standalone.observation: Premise is framed up front, but most beats compress an obscure tale into one dense line; following requires knowing both the Grimm original and wrestling slang.

performer.observation: A consistent wrestling-commentator diction (heat, pushed, botched, screwjob) and a few color-commentary asides give a voice, but delivery stays flat and uniform across nearly 60 beats.

storyBetweenCards.observation: Recurring motifs (the turnip line reused, salad/Rampion/Rapunzel chain, the heel bookend) connect cards, but the sequence is still a catalog march, not a developing plot.

individuality.observation: Specific, often obscure tale choices and precise textual quotes mapped onto wrestling terms feel researched and particular, not a generic fairy-tale-parody template.

outro.observation: The heel/installment callback pays off the opening joke, but "Stay Fluffy, Folks!" is an unmotivated sign-off with no setup anywhere in this text.

transferable.observation: Each line is tied to a specific tale's plot detail and quote; the content itself, not just a reusable frame, carries the piece.

flags.observation: "this load hurts my shoulder; horse, cow, pig, then just a stone" has no attached wrestling term, breaking the jargon pattern used in neighboring beats.
"The Cat of Kehrewit" names a very obscure tale with no contextual cue, likely unrecognized by most listeners.
Ends on a question ("have we not reason to weep?") rather than the declarative punch used elsewhere, breaking the established rhythm.
The lyric itself labels the line "reused", naming its own repetition rather than letting the callback work unannounced.
"Black Friday!" inserts a modern retail reference into the Grimm/wrestling frame with no bridge explaining the association.
"Stay Fluffy, Folks!" has no antecedent anywhere earlier in the text; "Fluffy" is unexplained within these three files.
